question: What is the main goal of family planning right after delivery?

options.B: Ensuring the immediate return of normal menstruation
options.C: Speeding up the physical involution of the uterus
options.D: Preventing closely spaced and unplanned pregnancies

explanation: Postpartum family planning helps mothers space out their pregnancies, giving their bodies time to recover and protecting the health of both mom and baby! You've got this.

question: Why is it important to talk about contraception early after birth, even before periods return?

options.A: Hormonal changes permanently stop ovulation for at least one year
options.B: Lactation guarantees complete protection against any future pregnancy
options.C: Menstruation always returns exactly six weeks after delivery
options.D: Fertility can return before the first postpartum menstrual period

explanation: Ovulation often happens before a mother sees her first period after birth. Knowing this helps us guide new mums safely!

question: Why do we usually avoid estrogen-containing pills for mothers who are breastfeeding?

options.A: They can significantly reduce the breast milk supply
options.B: They transfer directly into breast milk as a heavy poison
options.C: They stimulate excessive and painful uterine contractions
options.D: They always cause immediate cessation of all lochia

explanation: Estrogen can lower milk volume. That is why progestin-only options or non-hormonal methods are much safer choices for nursing mums early on.

question: A mum who is exclusively breastfeeding her 2-month-old baby asks about natural birth control. What is required for the Lactational Amenorrhea Method (LAM) to work?

options.A: She must have experienced at least two normal menstrual cycles
options.B: She must practice exclusive breastfeeding and remain without menses
options.C: She must pump breast milk at least four times every night
options.D: She must supplement feeds with formula every night

explanation: LAM is a wonderful natural method, but it relies strictly on exclusive breastfeeding, a baby under six months, and no returned period yet.

question: Which family planning method also protects against sexually transmitted infections (STIs)?
explanation: Condoms and other barrier methods are great because they do double duty: they prevent pregnancy and block infections too!

question: What is the biggest perk of long-acting reversible contraceptives (LARCs) like IUDs?

options.A: They stop postpartum weight gain and stabilize mood swings instantly
options.B: They protect the client completely against all types of infections
options.C: They permanently eliminate the need for any future medical checkups
options.D: They provide years of reliable protection without daily user action

explanation: LARCs are super convenient because once they are in place, the client does not have to remember a daily pill.

question: When should a nurse refer a postpartum mother to a specialized family planning clinic?

options.A: When a new mother refuses to hold her baby after a normal delivery
options.B: When routine postpartum lochia transitions from red to yellow-white
options.C: When the infant develops mild neonatal jaundice in the first week
options.D: When a client has a complex medical history requiring expert evaluation

explanation: Mums with underlying health conditions like severe high blood pressure need expert guidance to pick the safest contraceptive method.

question: Which of these is a normal finding and NOT a reason to refer a client to a special clinic?

options.A: Routine spontaneous passage of small lochial blood clots
options.B: Underlying chronic illness requiring careful risk assessment
options.C: History of severe adverse side effects with previous pills
options.D: Desire for long-acting reversible contraception like an implant

explanation: Passing small blood clots early in the postpartum period is totally normal and expected, so it does not need a special referral.

question: What does non-directive counseling mean when helping a client choose birth control?

options.A: Providing unbiased information to help the client choose freely
options.B: Refusing to answer any questions about hormonal side effects
options.C: Allowing the doctor to make all final decisions for the client
options.D: Telling the client which contraceptive method she must use

explanation: As nurses, our role is to give clear, unbiased facts so the client can make her own empowered choice. No pressure!

question: A client is scared that birth control pills will cause permanent infertility. How should you respond?

options.A: Explain that fertility typically returns shortly after stopping the pills
options.B: Tell her to ignore her worries and take the medication anyway
options.C: Agree that most modern contraceptives ruin a woman's womb forever
options.D: Refer her immediately to surgery without giving any explanation

explanation: Myths can cause a lot of worry! Patiently clearing up doubts with warm, accurate facts helps clients feel safe and informed.

question: What key details must be included when writing a family planning referral note?

options.A: A detailed financial breakdown of the hospital delivery bill
options.B: The baby's exact birth weight recorded in ounces and pounds
options.C: Relevant obstetric history and the specific reason for referral
options.D: The nurse's personal home address and phone contact details

explanation: The receiving clinic needs a clear picture of the mother's health history and why she was sent so they can give her the best care.

question: Why is it helpful to properly prepare a client before she visits the family planning clinic?

options.A: It prevents the clinic staff from asking her any personal questions
options.B: It reduces anxiety and increases the likelihood she will attend
options.C: It eliminates the need for any further medical history taking
options.D: It guarantees that she will receive free services at the facility

explanation: When clients know what to expect and where to go, they feel much more confident and are way more likely to show up!

question: How can a nurse help a client who is struggling with transportation to a clinic appointment?

options.A: Connecting her with affordable clinic options or community support
options.B: Telling her that missing the appointment has no health consequences
options.C: Insisting that she buy a personal vehicle before discharge
options.D: Advising her to walk several miles alone in the hot afternoon sun

explanation: Practical problems like transport can stop mums from getting care. Helping them find nearby or affordable options makes a huge difference.

question: You previously referred a postpartum mother for family planning. During her baby's immunization visit, what should you do?

options.A: Assume she went and make no further mention of the referral
options.B: Scold her publicly for failing to attend the scheduled appointment
options.C: Resend the exact same referral letter without speaking to her
options.D: Ask the client if she successfully visited the family planning clinic

explanation: Following up during routine visits shows you care and helps ensure she gets the support she needs for her family goals.
